summary:
Held 1 of today's 10 biggest US movers.

• 6 upside misses — DLTR +11%, CSGP +8%, MRNA +7%, CHTR +6%, NKE +6%. These cleared the universe screen but no strategy picked them up; the morning brief either filtered them on a catalyst/RSI/earnings rule or had nothing positive to trigger an entry.

• 3 downside moves (ADI -17%, HPE -16%, SNDK -14%) are unreachable on a long-only basket — no mechanism to express a short or pair-trade.

• Most instructive miss: ADI (-17.37%) — FQ4 earnings beat (rev ~$4.37B, EPS $4.06), but the stock sold off hard on FY27 capex of $1.6–1.9B, expected gross-margin moderation, and in-line Q1 guidance. Reports date the drop to Nov 24 or 25. Why we passed: Outside any active strategy's universe: ADI is a large-cap semiconductor name that no strategy lists. It was also an earnings-gap move, so pre-market positioning would have beaten any post-result momentum or mean-reversion signal. The bot is long-only, so it can't short the drop.

top_movers.catalyst: Q3 earnings beat: adj. EPS $1.16 above consensus, revenue +6.9% to ~$5.07B, comps +4.6% on traffic +3.8%, and raised FY guidance. Discount retailers rallied with it.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe (mid/large-cap discount retailer). It was also a pre-market earnings gap, so post-open momentum or news signals entered after most of the +11% move had happened.
top_movers.suggestion: Add DLTR and similar consumer-staples/discount retail names to the news-reactive universe, and let the earnings gate release names with a gap ≥ +5% on a beat-and-raise within 15 minutes of the open.

top_movers.catalyst: No obvious news catalyst found for 2026-11-25. Searches only returned earlier 2026 CSGP moves (Homes AI launch, analyst target hikes), so this is likely a rebound or sector move.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: CSGP is a mid-cap real-estate data/software name that no strategy includes. With no discrete catalyst, a news-reactive trigger had nothing to fire on.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a liquidity-screened 'high-beta rebound' watchlist (e.g. mid-caps down >40% YTD with avg dollar volume >$100M) to the momentum universe, so ≥+5% gap-up days on volume ≥1.5× average can trigger entries.

top_movers.catalyst: no obvious news catalyst found for 2026-11-25 — likely sector/biotech momentum or sentiment-driven move; search surfaced no same-day Moderna headline.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: MRNA is a volatile, headline-driven mid-cap biotech, a category the momentum, mean-reversion and news strategies don't include. With no clear catalyst, a news-reactive bot had nothing to trigger on either.
top_movers.suggestion: (no actionable change — a +7% move without a catalyst in a name outside the universe doesn't justify adding high-beta biotech; at most, add a watchlist alert for names whose daily move is ≥ +7% on ≥2× average volume.)

top_movers.catalyst: No confirmed catalyst for 2026-11-25: searches returned nothing dated that day. Likely a sector or sentiment move, possibly tied to the SpaceX mobile-partnership talk that drove June's rally.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. CHTR is a mid/large-cap cable and broadband name, and no strategy includes it. With no identifiable pre-market catalyst, a news-reactive bot had no trigger either.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a daily 'unexplained top-gainer' watchlist, such as US names with >+5% moves on >1.5x average volume across S&P 500/400 constituents, so the universe filter stops excluding large caps like CHTR.

top_movers.catalyst: no obvious news catalyst found for 2026-11-25 — likely a sector or consumer-discretionary rotation or a rebound in a depressed name (close of $35.75 is far below historical levels).
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: NKE is a large-cap consumer-discretionary name that no strategy includes. With no discrete catalyst, a news-reactive signal had nothing to trigger on, and a +5.9% move on rotation would not pass a gap filter.
top_movers.suggestion: Add large-cap consumer-discretionary names (NKE, LULU, etc.) to the momentum-trader universe, gated by a relative-strength filter such as 1-day return ≥ +4% with volume ≥ 1.5× its 20-day average.

top_movers.catalyst: No obvious news catalyst found for 2026-11-25. Searches returned only older IP upgrade and investor-day stories, so this is likely a sector or technical move (packaging/materials).
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. IP is a mid/large-cap packaging and materials name that no strategy's universe includes. With no identifiable news catalyst, a news-reactive filter would also have had nothing to trigger on.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a low-cost 'unlisted mover' watch to the universe builder: auto-include S&P 500 names with a >=5% gain on >=1.5x average volume for next-day momentum screening. A sector-ETF relative-strength check could separate sector moves from stock-specific ones.

top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: ADI is a large-cap semiconductor name that no strategy lists. It was also an earnings-gap move, so pre-market positioning would have beaten any post-result momentum or mean-reversion signal. The bot is long-only, so it can't short the drop.
top_movers.suggestion: Add large-cap semis such as ADI, TXN and MCHP to the mean-reversion universe, and let an earnings-gate release names with a gap down of 10% or more on a beat, entering only after a stabilisation bar in the first hour.

top_movers.catalyst: FQ4 beat and raised revenue outlook, but Cloud & AI margin guided to ~14% for FY27 (vs 18.4%) on memory costs and supply limits. Stock fell 16%, its worst day since 2015. Reported Nov 24, so possibly a day-after move.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: HPE is a large-cap IT hardware name that no strategy lists. It was also an earnings gap-down on a margin-guidance surprise, which a long-only momentum or mean-reversion bot has no way to trade.
top_movers.suggestion: Add large-cap hardware/AI-infrastructure names like HPE, DELL and SMCI to the mean-reversion universe, with an earnings-gap-down rule that buys only after a ≥10% drop plus a day-2 stabilization close above the day-1 low.

top_movers.catalyst: No confirmed Nov 25 catalyst. Searches found only earlier-November SNDK drops (Nov 10 and 13) tied to an AI-hardware/memory sell-off and NAND share worries, so this is likely a continuation of that sector move.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: SNDK is a recently spun-off, highly volatile mid-cap NAND/memory name that no strategy lists. Its multi-day double-digit slides would also trip typical gap, volatility and RSI filters, and a bot with no short capability can't act on a loser.
top_movers.suggestion: Add SNDK and similar high-beta AI-memory names (MU, WDC, STX) to the mean-reversion universe with a volatility cap, so a -14% day after consecutive drops can trigger an oversold-bounce entry once RSI(2) is below 10.

top_movers.catalyst: Post-earnings selloff after Q3 FY27: record revenue and a $132B AI backlog, but guidance for Q4 ISG operating margin fell to just under 15% and AI-server margins looked compressed.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside the universe of the momentum and mean-reversion strategies. The move was an earnings gap on results released after the prior close, so it was priced at the open. Only the news-reactive strategies trade DELL, and they didn't take a position.
top_movers.suggestion: Add DELL to the momentum universe, or add an earnings-day rule so a post-earnings gap ≤ -8% on ≥2× average volume is eligible for mean-reversion entry after a 30-minute stabilization window.
